name: May logistic generation map
description: Normalized discrete-generation logistic map X[n+1]=r*X[n]*(1-X[n]), with synchronous old-state updates and exactly one generation per Euler step. Illustrative default r=3.9,X[0]=0.1; companion scenario presets r=3.7, 3.8, 3.9 preserve the three legacy default populations without three catalog mechanisms. This is a mathematical teaching example, not a calibrated ecological forecast. Use only Euler,dt=discrete_period=1 and whole generations. Diagnostic Instantaneous Log Slope is one iterate's log(abs(r*(1-2*X))), not a long-run Lyapunov estimate; Coarse Parameter Range Code is an interval label and 99 does not establish chaos. Periodic windows occur above 3.57. Presets: use r=3.7, 3.8 or 3.9 with Population=0.1 over 0..100 whole generations; keep Euler and dt=discrete_period=1. To try a case, open Inspect, select r under Equations & initial values, change its Equation in the existing editor, then Run. This intentionally changes the current draft; Save is separate. To compare, run and Save Run for 3.7, then 3.8, then 3.9 and use Compare; generated run labels follow that order, so retain parameter notes/exports. Former May's Logistic Map Model (may-logistic-chaos,r=3.7) and May Ecological Chaos Model (may-ecological-chaos-eco,r=3.8) are these parameter cases, not separate mechanisms. Agents can use compare_scenarios with model_id may-chaos-population-eco and named parameters r/Population; use the published preset payload when available. Instantaneous log slope is not an averaged Lyapunov exponent, and coarse interval code 99 does not prove chaos. JSON preserves the generation contract; unsupported XMILE export explains choosing JSON. Migration notes: former model IDs may-logistic-chaos (r=3.7) and may-ecological-chaos-eco (r=3.8) map to this retained canonical ID plus those parameter presets. Their originals are archived; old direct links are not automatically redirected. Existing saved/private copies are not changed. For exact old report columns use the documented preset-specific compatibility mapping, since Growth_Rate had different meanings in the two variants.

variables.name: Coarse Parameter Range Code
variables.equation: IF r < 1 THEN 0 ELSE IF r < 3 THEN 1 ELSE IF r < 3.449 THEN 2 ELSE IF r < 3.57 THEN 4 ELSE 99

reference: May RM. Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics. Nature. 1976;261:459-467.
